reviews.reason: changes: the Protected documents section gains a gap-pass paragraph (owner, 2026-11-13) and two rules the review of that paragraph asked for. The gap pass: a protected review also names the rule, case or claim the document leaves unstated, as numbered findings with a recommendation and a cost; a gap finding is a proposal that always parks for the owner, because it would add a rule the owner has never owned; an accepted finding is re-reviewed once and the hash records the final bytes; a housekeeping finding may be applied and re-reviewed; every disposition is recorded with the round and restated here. Completeness: a review is complete only when the hash-matched bytes and the gap pass come from the same qualifying seat - the seat reads the bytes, the parent recomputes the hash and the guard trip-wires it, so a seat without a shell is not thereby partial - and a partial review parks, naming the missing half. Membership: a document joins the set when it owns a non-negotiable or a repo delta of the canonical skill, not because of its directory; a runbook or research note is not governing, the seat files under .opencode/agents are operational, the parent proposes and the owner confirms, and the three lists move together. why: two protected reviews earlier today found contradictions but nobody had been asked for absences, and absences are what a protected document prevents; the set itself had three hardcoded lists with nothing keeping them in step. rejected: applying gap findings as part of the review (the landed text would differ from the reviewed bytes); letting auto-accept cover a gap finding (the reviewer would author governance); a second unbounded re-review loop; making the seat recompute the hash (its shell is denied in every review). Gap dispositions: 1 (auto-accept could land an owner-unseen rule) and 3 (no recorded disposition) applied in the first pass; 2 (a partial review should park) and 4 (the set can drift) applied in this pass, with the hash-recompute ambiguity the review flagged resolved in the text; 5 (AGENTS.md section 10a lacks the one-confirmation bound) carried to its own protected round; E (a test that the three lists agree) carried to the backlog, because the owner kept the guard as it is.
reviews.attestation: On the pro seat deepseek-v4-pro:0813 (outside the 12:00-18:00 window) I read the exact landing text and ran the gap pass the paragraph describes. Round 1 found the safety valve would never fire on the case it created (a gap finding names an unowned rule); the fix made a gap finding a proposal that always parks, with housekeeping applied and re-reviewed. Round 2 accepted that and raised the completeness and membership gaps the owner then took; round 3 reviewed those amendments and found the hash-recompute ambiguity (a seat without a shell would be a partial review under a strict reading) and the off-axis membership example, both fixed in the final pass, which a confirmation accepted. The reviewer could not recompute the hash (shell denied), which is the case the text now covers; the recorded value is the parent recomputation and tests/meta/protected-doc-review.test.ts is the tripwire. Made no edits, ran no gates, committed nothing. Any later edit to the text must be re-reviewed and re-recorded.
